# Campfire SMS

> Campfire SMS is a hosted two-way SMS bridge for AI agents, available for US and Canadian mobile numbers. It is a published ChatGPT plugin. With Grok Bot webhook wake configured, an incoming text triggers a cloud routine that retrieves the message and can reply by SMS while the user’s PC is off. Active local-agent connections are also supported.

## Product facts

Campfire SMS operates phone enrollment, SMS delivery, the authenticated message queue, and routing. The connected agent supplies the model, tools, project access, and task execution. The phone needs SMS service; mobile data and a separate chat app are not required for texting.

The local connector adds messaging to the agent's existing workspace. It does not require a Campfire SMS coding project, repository import, or a second coding model. Account verification and connector configuration are still required.

### ChatGPT plugin

Campfire SMS is published as a ChatGPT plugin. The user installs it from its ChatGPT plugin page (https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad15caa12d08191b5663247ed3d583a) or by searching Plugins (or Apps) in ChatGPT, then signs in with their verified phone number and Campfire SMS PIN to connect; no local install is needed. In ordinary chats and Work chats, ChatGPT can open a bridge, text the user, check and acknowledge replies, and close the bridge. Ordinary chats read replies only when ChatGPT next checks. A Work chat (ChatGPT web, or the desktop app with Cloud selected) can subscribe to the `sms.received` MCP event so an SMS reply resumes the task; one subscription per open bridge, lasting up to seven days. Event payloads carry IDs only; ChatGPT never receives the phone number. ChatGPT asks for approval before sending a text ("Allow ChatGPT to use Campfire SMS?"); choosing Always allow avoids a send waiting while the user is away. A text cannot start a new ChatGPT chat.

### Grok Bot webhook wake

Connect the hosted Streamable HTTP MCP at `https://api.campfiresms.com/mcp` with a per-installation bearer in the host’s secure credential settings. Create an active webhook-triggered routine on the owning Bot, then save its URL and sender key in the Campfire SMS account’s Grok Bot 24/7 wake panel. One installation owns wake per account.

An incoming SMS queues a message and wake job. The webhook event contains an event name, delivery ID, and bridge ID; the SMS body stays in the authenticated MCP queue. Grok’s cloud routine opens or reuses the bridge, retrieves pending messages, handles them, acknowledges handled IDs, and can send an SMS reply. A routine can run while the user’s PC is off. This does not start a stopped local coding-agent session.

A successful webhook probe confirms run acceptance only. Verify a real SMS → webhook run → authenticated message retrieval → SMS reply before treating a setup as working. Duplicate wakes with an empty message queue should finish quietly.

### Local-agent connections

Codex, Grok Build, Claude Code, OpenCode, and other compatible MCP or HTTP API hosts can send updates and retrieve replies during active work. For a local connector, keep the computer awake and online with the agent running. Installation alone does not schedule checks or wake stopped sessions. Local scheduled workflows require an available runtime.

SMS instructions stay within the agent’s existing permissions. Native approvals remain in its environment. Campfire SMS does not run an additional AI model. SMS is not end-to-end encrypted; keep credentials and sensitive information out of texts.

## Enrollment and local setup

Start with human phone verification. For hosted MCP, use the account’s one-time command with `--credential-only`; this enrollment step needs Node.js 18+ but no Python or pip. Transfer the stored credential only into the host’s secure credential field.

For local installation, use Node.js 18+ and Python 3.12+. The installer can register detected Codex and Grok Build CLIs; other compatible hosts require their own MCP configuration. On Linux or a VM, run as the same non-root user as the agent, create and activate a Python virtual environment before setup, and configure MCP with its absolute Python path. Do not use sudo pip, system pip, or --break-system-packages.

See [local setup](https://campfiresms.com/install.html#local-agents) and [Linux/VM instructions](https://campfiresms.com/install.html#linux-vm).

- [Home](https://campfiresms.com/): Grok webhook wake, one SMS example, and current pricing and message counting.
- [ChatGPT SMS](https://campfiresms.com/chatgpt-sms/): The Campfire SMS ChatGPT plugin: texts from ChatGPT, replies, ordinary chat vs Work reply wake, the approval prompt, pricing, and privacy.
- [Set up Campfire SMS in ChatGPT](https://campfiresms.com/guides/chatgpt-sms-plugin.html): Step-by-step plugin install, phone + PIN connection, first text, replies, Work wake subscription, disconnecting, and fixes.
- [Text Grok Bot about any task, even with your PC off](https://campfiresms.com/guides/grok-bot-sms-routine.html): Everyday and coding tasks by SMS. Hosted MCP, webhook routine, secure wake configuration, and a real text-and-reply test.
- [Setup](https://campfiresms.com/install.html): ChatGPT plugin, Grok Bot, then local-agent installation, recovery, and removal. US and Canadian mobile numbers only for now.
- [Troubleshooting and FAQ](https://campfiresms.com/troubleshooting/): Supported countries (US and Canada), ChatGPT replies and bridge conflicts, iPhone replies marked Not Delivered, missing replies, “No agent bridge is connected,” credential errors, Grok Bot wake, and message limits.
- [Guides](https://campfiresms.com/guides/): Grok wake setup and supporting local-agent workflows.
- [NudgeBell vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/nudgebell-vs-campfiresms/): Scheduled reminders and escalation versus two-way agent SMS, with sources and runtime requirements.
- [AgentPhone vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/agentphone-vs-campfiresms/): Phone numbers, voice, and verification codes for agents, compared with your existing agent texting you. Checked with dated pricing.
- [AgentCall vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/agentcall-vs-campfiresms/): Agent phone numbers, AI voice, OTP extraction, and relay mode (which needs a webhook the agent hosts) versus a hosted bridge with no webhook.
- [textbee vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/textbee-vs-campfiresms/): Same-direction agent notifications from your own Android phone and SIM (open source) versus a hosted bridge with no phone app or gateway device.
- [Sendblue vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/sendblue-vs-campfiresms/): iMessage API for customer-facing agents and sales versus SMS between you and the agent you already run.
- [CallMeMCP (/call-me) vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/callmemcp-vs-campfiresms/): An iPhone app that lets agents ring you and transcribes your spoken answer, versus SMS to your own number on any phone with no app. Checked with dated App Store pricing.
- [ntfy vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/ntfy-vs-campfiresms/): Free, open-source push alerts wired up with a hook (no chat reply; http action buttons need an endpoint you host) versus two-way texts with your agent.
- [Pushover vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/pushover-vs-campfiresms/): One-time-purchase one-way alerts (emergency acknowledgement is not an answer) versus texts your agent can read back.
- [Claude Code Telegram plugin vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/telegram-vs-campfiresms/): Claude Code's free channels plugin (bot, Bun, open session, tool-approval relay, Claude Code only) versus SMS from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, and Grok Bot.
- [Ways to hear from your AI coding agent](https://campfiresms.com/coding-agent-notification-options/): Campfire SMS, /call-me, the Claude Code Telegram plugin, ntfy, Pushover, and DIY Twilio compared on replies, supported agents, setup, and dated pricing.
- [MCP SMS notifications](https://campfiresms.com/mcp-sms-notifications/): Send, retrieve, and acknowledge tools, setup routes, and a complete reply test.
- [Build completion SMS](https://campfiresms.com/build-complete-sms/): Have an active agent report build, test, or evaluation results and handle follow-up questions.
- [Pull request SMS notifications](https://campfiresms.com/pull-request-sms-notifications/): Agent-observed PR readiness, summaries, and reply handling; setup alone does not watch GitHub events.
- [When an agent needs input](https://campfiresms.com/agent-needs-input/): Human clarification by SMS within existing authorization, with a waiting window and fallback.
- [Agent notifications vs reminders](https://campfiresms.com/agent-notifications-vs-reminders/): Event alerts, durable scheduling, human acknowledgment, task replies, and runtime availability.
- [Codex SMS](https://campfiresms.com/codex-sms/): Add SMS to the existing Codex repository and runtime, with setup and a reply test.
- [Claude Code SMS](https://campfiresms.com/claude-code-sms/): Register the local MCP connector with an existing Claude Code environment.
- [Codex phone notifications](https://campfiresms.com/codex-phone-notifications/): Define completion, blocker, and decision alerts for an active task.
- [Claude Code phone notifications](https://campfiresms.com/claude-code-phone-notifications/): Set useful SMS update rules and retrieve replies.
- [Remote Codex](https://campfiresms.com/remote-control-codex/): Compare short SMS steering, SSH, remote desktop, and a hosted agent.
- [Claude Code Remote Control vs SMS](https://campfiresms.com/remote-control-claude-code/): Compare a native remote session view and SMS while keeping the local workspace.
- [Phone task decisions and native approvals](https://campfiresms.com/approve-coding-agent-from-phone/): SMS replies clarify tasks but do not replace native permission approvals.
- [Photon vs Campfire SMS](https://campfiresms.com/photon-vs-campfiresms/): Project-based messaging SDK setup versus a focused connection to the existing coding workflow. Photon can also integrate into an application the developer owns.
- [iMessage vs SMS for coding agents](https://campfiresms.com/imessage-vs-sms-coding-agents/): Compare messaging interfaces and separate channel choice from agent runtime availability.
